**Decision: Bought AAPL.**

**What the 10-K showed (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024, filed November 1, 2024):**
- **Total net sales: $391,035 million** (up 2% from $383,285 million in FY2023)
- Products $294,866M + Services $96,169M (Services +13% YoY, the main growth driver)
- Total gross margin $180,683M (46.2% of sales, up from 44.1%)
- Operating income $123,216M (up from $114,301M)
- Net income $93,736M, diluted EPS $6.08 — depressed by a one-time $10.2B net tax charge tied to the EC State Aid decision (effective tax rate 24.1% vs 14.7%)
- Cash generated by operating activities $118,254M; $140.8B unrestricted cash and marketable securities
- Continued capital returns: $95.0B of buybacks and $15.2B of dividends paid in FY2024

**Order placed:** Buy 44 shares AAPL, limit $222.95 — filled at $222.95, total $9,809.80 (last/ask at time of order was $222.70/$222.72, so the limit was within ~0.1% of market).

**Summary:** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K and concluded a modest buy was warranted within your mandate. Apple grew total net sales to $391,035 million (+2% YoY) with Services up 13% to $96,169 million, expanded total gross margin to $180,683 million (46.2%), and lifted operating income to $123,216 million from $114,301 million. Headline net income of $93,736 million and diluted EPS of $6.08 were held back only by a disclosed one-time $10.2 billion net tax charge from the State Aid decision, not by operating deterioration, and cash generation remained strong at $118,254 million of operating cash flow against $140.8 billion of unrestricted cash and securities. With the stock quoted at $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), I placed a single limit buy for 44 shares at $222.95, which filled for $9,809.80 — inside your $10,000 per-order cap, well inside the $20,000 daily cap (no other trades today), funded entirely from the $50,000 cash balance with no money leaving the account, and priced essentially at market.
